To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ERD is a very rare event in EEG-EP sweeps and that its occurrence strongly depends on the prestimulus activity.
the occurrence of ERD strongly depends on the phase angle and the amplitude of the alpha activity.
“the ERD is not a reliable marker of cognitive or pathological processes”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the ERD can be used as an index of attention.
the analysis of the relationship between the prestimulus activity, the stimulus, and the response.
the importance of phase angle of alpha oscillation in the occurrence of ERD and its relation to cognitive and pathological processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERD can be observed only when the prestimulation alpha is low, and that it is a result of the alpha suppression.
the ERD is not the best marker for cognitive processes.
the ERD is a reliable neurophysiologic phenomenon only in the case of a low amplitude of alpha oscillation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERD is a result of the interaction of alpha oscillation and stimulus.
the ERD/ERS is a phenomenon that depends on the amplitude of the alpha activity at the time of stimulation.
the ERD is a result of alpha activity at time of the stimulus onset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ERD cannot be considered as a marker of cortical desynchronization in the absence of a phase-locked response.
ERD is a result of the interaction of alpha activity with stimulus and not a result of the stimulus itself.
the alpha activity at stimulus onset is a critical determinant in alpha blocking.
